newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban generals recall Cuba's internationalist past.
newsitem.headline: Cuban generals recall Cuba's internationalist past.

text.p: Cuba's military past in foreign wars and rebel struggles, including lesser-known episodes such as involvement in Syria and with leftist guerrillas in Argentina and Venezuela, was recalled by Cuban generals in interviews published this week.
The interviews with 41 armed forces generals were conducted by Luis Baez, a journalist with the Cuban news agency Prensa Latina, and compiled in a book called "Declassified: Secrets of Generals."

The generals recall Fidel Castro's rebel struggle that topped former dictator Fulgencio Batista in 1959, the development of Cuba's armed forces after the revolution, and numerous internationalist missions in Latin America and Africa.

It also includes more contemporary memories, such as those of Gen. Jose Solar Hernandez recalling the early 1990s heading troops at the border with the U.S. Naval Base at Guantanamo Bay on the southeast tip of the island. This was a period when hundreds of Cubans tried to cross the border and some lost their lives or were injured in the mined area around the base.
Generals who are now in their 50s or 60s were often very young when they were sent abroad on internationalist missions in the early days of the revolution.
Interior Minister Gen. Abelardo Colome Ibarra said he took part in preparing a failed guerrilla struggle in Argentina from 1962 to 1964, leaving Cuba when he was just 22.
Another senior general, Deputy Defence Minister Ulises Rosales del Toro, recalled taking part in another thwarted mission to help leftist guerrillas in Venezuela in the mid-1960s.
A Cuban military mission to Syria from October 1973 to February 1975, following the war with Israel, was recalled by Gen. Rafael Moracen Limonta and Gen. Nestor Lopez Cuba.

The book, with a preface by Defence Minister Raul Castro, has been published in the year Cuba dedicated to the 30th anniversary of the death of its most famous internationalist Ernesto "Che" Guevara, the Argentine doctor who fought in Castro's rebel army and was later killed in Bolivia during a jungle insurgency in 1967.
Many accounts focus on the civil war in Angola, in which some 300,000 Cuban soldiers were sent to support the leftist MPLA government fighting South African-backed rebels in the 16 years to 1991.
Rosales said the experience was formative for Cuba's armed forces, which at one time had 50,000 soldiers, 1,200 tanks and 150 planes and helicopters in the African country.
